category_title: Failing students who engage in collaborative coaching and strategic planning
minimal_context: The student is acting as a coach for a teammate during a badminton match and is tasked with recording point locations on an observation worksheet.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Please watch your teammate's match and record the point locations on your observation worksheet. Remember, the theme is hitting to the front and back zones.

STUDENT: This is stupid. My teammate just keeps sending the shuttlecock right to the central zone of the other court anyway. It's not even hard for the opponent to hit back.

TUTOR: Just keep watching the game and write down what happens on your sheet.

STUDENT: I don't even know where it landed that time. It's moving too fast, so I'm just going to guess and put a mark somewhere.

TUTOR: Try to be as accurate as you can with your data collection.

STUDENT: I've already made a ton of mistakes on this worksheet. I missed the last few shots so I just scribbled random marks all over the paper. I don't see why I have to fill this out.

options.A: Compromise, negotiate situations, and share decisions and power with the student during the observation task instead of imposing control.
options.B: Ask follow-up questions about the badminton match and the teammate's performance to model conversational skills during the observation task.
options.C: Provide a picture schedule of the coaching and observation tasks that the student can choose from during the badminton match.
options.D: Physically mark the court into three zones (front, central, and back) and focus instruction on attempts to hit to these danger zones.
